title: SDK Sandbox Telemetry: Redaction & Sampling Guidelines
author: Amara Singh
body:
Summary
This guide describes the recommended telemetry policy for developer sandboxes and local SDK test environments. It focuses on three operational goals: protect PII and customer secrets, keep event volume bounded (cost-control), and preserve signal for debugging. The guidance applies to SDKs (JS, Python, Go) and the local emulation/preview proxies used by developer workflows.

Why this doc exists
- Developer sandboxes commonly leak sensitive tokens and full prompt text into telemetry.
- Unbounded sandbox traffic (long prompts, embed-heavy tests) inflates costs and noise for analytics.
- Observability needs for debugging (trace IDs, error classes) must be preserved while maintaining compliance.

When to apply
1) Local dev containers and ephemeral sandboxes (env: DEV, SANDBOX).
2) Preview environments: staging-for-features that mirror customer flows but use synthetic data.
3) CI jobs that run customer-like prompts (limit sampling).

Principles
- Default-deny for free-text fields: redact by default unless whitelisted.
- Telemetry must never include: full prompt text, API keys, entitlement tokens, customer PII (ssn, cc numbers), or private URLs.
- Preserve structured signal: model_name, model_version, response_latency_ms, error_code, trace_id, bucketed_token_count.
- Use deterministic hashing for consistent but irreversible IDs (e.g., sha256(prompt) truncated).

Policy summary table
| Field Type | Sandbox Default | Notes |
|------------|-----------------|-------|
| prompt_text | REDACTED | Replace with hash and token_count bucket |
| request_headers | REDACTED except: X-Request-ID | Remove auth headers, keep routing headers |
| response_tokens | BUCKETED (0-50,51-200,200+) | Numeric buckets only |
| embeddings_payload | STRIPPED | Send metadata (size, vector_dim) only |
| api_key | DROP | Must never be sent |
| trace_id | KEEP | Required for cross-service debug |

Redaction rules (deterministic)
1) Free-text fields: replace with "[REDACTED_FREE_TEXT_HASH:<short-hash>]" and include token_count_bucket. Example: prompt_text -> "[REDACTED_FREE_TEXT_HASH:ab12cd] tokens=51-200"
2) URLs: If host matches an allowlist (internal redwood-test.example), keep host path cleared (only domain and path length). Otherwise replace with "[REDACTED_URL]".
3) Numbers with >6 digits: redact 4 trailing digits and mark as "masked_number". Detect via regex groups.
4) Emails: retain domain only (user@example.com -> [redacted]@example.com).
5) Custom customer identifiers: apply HMAC-SHA256 with the environment key (not the API key) and truncate to 12 chars. Store mapping only in local ephemeral caches.

Sampling strategy (recommended defaults)
- Local Dev (DEV): sample_rate = 1% (0.01) for full error events, 10% for warning traces, 0% for full prompts.
- CI/Preflight: sample_rate = 5% full errors, 0% full prompts, retain only structured metrics.
- Preview Environments: sample_rate = 10% for traces, 100% for aggregated metrics (latency, token usage) but redacted payloads.
- Opt-in full capture: only by setting SDK env var REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_CAPTURE=full and with developer consent file present (telemetry-override.json in repo root).

SDK integration examples
1) Environment flags (all SDKs):
- REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE = sandbox | staging | production
- REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE = 0.01
- REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_REDACT_ENV_KEY = <env-hmac-key> (set in CI, never checked into git)

2) JS snippet (conceptual):
const telemetry = require('@redwood/telemetry-sdk');
telemetry.configure({ mode: process.env.REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE || 'sandbox', sampleRate: parseFloat(process.env.REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE || '0.01'), redactKey: process.env.REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_REDACT_ENV_KEY });

3) Python example (conceptual):
from redwood_telemetry import Telemetry
T = Telemetry(mode=os.getenv('REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE','sandbox'), sample_rate=float(os.getenv('REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE','0.01')), redact_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_REDACT_ENV_KEY'))

Telemetry event contract (sandbox-safe)
{
  "event_type": "string",
  "timestamp": "ISO8601",
  "trace_id": "string",
  "model": "string",
  "model_version": "string",
  "token_count_bucket": "string",
  "latency_ms": "number",
  "error_code": "string|null",
  "prompt_hash": "string|null",
  "extra": {"note": "short string, no free-text longer than 200 chars"}
}
Note: In the file above, the extra map must be limited to short strings. SDK should enforce max_len=200 and automatically truncate.

Enforcement checklist for SDK authors
1) Implement redaction pipeline in client before any network calls to telemetry endpoint.
2) Validate removal of Authorization or any header with "token" or "key" in name.
3) Add unit tests for each redaction rule (regex-based).
4) Add fuzz tests to ensure extremely long prompt inputs do not bypass redaction.
5) Add CI gating: Telemetry smoke test runs with mode=sandbox and asserts no free-text fields in captured payloads.

Rollout plan for changes to production capture
1) Design: author PR with documentation and unit tests.
2) Canary: enable in 1% of developer sandbox traffic for 48 hours. Monitor false positive redactions (support ticket trend) and debugability degradation metrics (time_to_root_cause).
3) Expand: 10% for 72 hours.
4) Enforce: default on for all non-prod modes; production mode keeps full capture unless customer opts in.

Operational runbook (common incidents)
- Symptom: developers complain they cannot see any prompt context in traces.
  Steps: Check env REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_MODE and REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_CAPTURE. Confirm redaction rules file version (telemetry-redaction-v*). If override present, rotate redact key and reset local caches.
- Symptom: CI job exceeds telemetry quotas.
  Steps: Lower REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE for CI to 0.005 and limit events to aggregated metrics only.

Metrics to monitor
- fraction_redacted_events (target >= 95% for sandbox)
- telemetry_ingest_rate_by_env (target CI < 100/day per repo)
- time_to_debug (monitor for increases after stricter redaction; alert if > 2x baseline)
- support_tickets_tagged_telemetry_loss (trend must be flat or decreasing)

Appendix: Common regex snippets (examples)
- Detect credit-card-like numbers: (?<!\d)(?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?|5[1-5][0-9]{14}|3[47][0-9]{13})(?!\d)
- Email capture for domain only: ([^@\s]+)@([^@\s]+) -> keep group 2 only
- Long numeric token detection: \b\d{7,}\b -> mask last 4 digits
